key_insight: A structure-preserving neural density functional can learn ion correlations in polymer electrolytes while respecting key physical symmetries and thermodynamic constraints, enabling accurate transfer across concentrations and geometries.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route to predict ionic structure and response in complex electrolyte devices, bridging molecular-scale simulation data to continuum-scale design models.
method: Trained on planar density and internal-force profiles from molecular dynamics.
Built to preserve spatial symmetries, thermodynamic integrability, and Noether identities.
Uses nonlinear density dependence to capture concentration-dependent ion correlations and screening behavior.
evidence_signal: The model predicts density profiles at an untrained salt concentration, bulk structure factors, and long-wavelength response, and outperforms three other neural density-functional architectures while remaining accurate with only a quarter of the training runs.
watch_item: Generalization is demonstrated on related electrolyte settings, but deployment in new chemistries or far-from-training regimes may still require retraining and careful validation.
paper_title: A structure-preserving neural density functional for the ions of a polymer electrolyte
